description: Given an n x n array of integers matrix, return the minimum sum of any falling path through matrix. A falling path starts at any element in the first row and chooses the element in the next row that is either directly below or diagonally left/right.
intuition: Imagine rain falling down the matrix - at each cell, the water came from one of three cells above it. DP tracks the cheapest path to reach each cell, and the answer is the cheapest endpoint in the last row.
approach: Use dynamic programming. For each cell in row i, the minimum path sum is matrix[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j-1], dp[i-1][j], dp[i-1][j+1]). Process row by row and return the minimum of the last row.
explanation:
1. Initialize dp with the first row values.
2. For each subsequent row, compute new_dp[j] = matrix[i][j] + min of dp[j-1], dp[j], dp[j+1].
3. Handle boundary cases (j=0 has no left, j=n-1 has no right).
4. After processing all rows, the answer is the minimum value in dp.
5. Only O(n) extra space is used by keeping just the previous row.
hints: This is a classic DP problem. Process row by row.
Each cell can be reached from at most 3 cells in the previous row.
Only the previous row is needed, so optimize space to O(n).
